title: The Practice Before the Pressure
headline: Why Pressure Reveals What You’ve Practiced
tagline: What you repeatedly practice today can become what you are increasingly ready to do tomorrow.
seo_title: Why Pressure Reveals What You've Practiced (Hebrews 5:14) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: "I don't know where that came from." Sometimes pressure reveals what has been practiced. A devotional for men on Hebrews 5:14 and training in godliness.
verse_text: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil.

scriptures.text: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil.

items: Pressure arrives quickly.
The phone rings.
Someone insults you.
Temptation walks into the room.
Someone you love disappoints you.
And suddenly something comes out of you.
Sometimes we say, “I don’t know where that came from.”
Maybe we should investigate.

blocks.text: Pressure often reveals what has been practiced.

items: Not always.
One isolated response should not become a complete verdict on someone’s character.
Exhaustion, illness, trauma and stress matter.
But repeated responses under pressure deserve attention.
Nobody waits until the championship game to develop muscle memory.
The musician doesn’t wait until the concert to learn the song.
Preparation happens before pressure.
The Battle Before the Battle may be the practice before the pressure.
You don’t wait for enormous wealth to learn generosity. Practice open-handedness now.
You don’t wait for devastating offense to learn forgiveness. Practice releasing smaller debts.
You don’t wait for public leadership to learn humility. Practice humility without a title.
You don’t wait for catastrophe to learn trust. Practice trust inside ordinary uncertainty.
You don’t wait until everything is collapsing to furnish your mind with Scripture.
Repetition becomes readiness.
The time to furnish your mind with truth is before the storm asks your mind for an interpretation.
Familiar is not sovereign. Through Christ, an old road does not have to remain your road.
